stem: The Gupta period is often described as the '________' of ancient India for its achievements in art, science and literature.
solution: The Gupta era is popularly called the 'Golden Age' of ancient India due to remarkable progress in many fields.

stem: The Gupta ruler celebrated in the Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription) composed by Harishena was:
solution: The Prayaga Prashasti, written by his court poet Harishena, praises the conquests of Samudragupta.

stem: Because of his many military conquests, Samudragupta is sometimes called the:
solution: For his numerous conquests, Samudragupta has been nicknamed the 'Napoleon of India' by some historians.

stem: The great poet and dramatist who wrote 'Abhijnanashakuntalam' and is linked to the Gupta court was:
solution: Kalidasa, author of Shakuntala and Meghaduta, was a celebrated poet-dramatist associated with the Gupta age.

stem: The famous mathematician-astronomer of this era, who explained eclipses and worked with the concept of zero, was:
solution: Aryabhata, author of the Aryabhatiya, made pioneering contributions to astronomy and mathematics, including work related to zero and the Earth's rotation.

stem: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II was:
solution: Fa-Hien (Faxian) travelled to India during Chandragupta II's reign and left an account of Gupta society.

stem: Chandragupta II, a powerful Gupta ruler, is also known by the title:
solution: Chandragupta II bore the title 'Vikramaditya' and his reign marked a high point of Gupta power and culture.

stem: The Indian numeral system with place value and the concept of zero, refined in this period, later spread to the world through the:
solution: The decimal place-value system and zero, developed in India, were transmitted to Europe largely through Arab scholars.

stem: The founder of the Gupta dynasty's rise to imperial power was Chandragupta I, who strengthened his position through:
options: A marriage alliance with the Lichchhavis
solution: CHANDRAGUPTA I strengthened the early Gupta position through a MARRIAGE ALLIANCE with the LICHCHHAVIS (a powerful clan), boosting the dynasty's prestige and power. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The capital of the Gupta empire was:
solution: The capital of the GUPTA empire was PATALIPUTRA (in Magadha) — the same city that had been the Mauryan capital. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta era is called a 'Golden Age' because of its achievements in:
options: Literature, art, science, mathematics and philosophy
solution: The GUPTA era is called a 'GOLDEN AGE' because of its remarkable achievements in LITERATURE (Kalidasa), ART (sculpture, painting), SCIENCE, MATHEMATICS (zero, decimals), and PHILOSOPHY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Aryabhata's contributions included stating that:
options: The Earth rotates on its axis and explaining the cause of eclipses
The Sun goes round the Earth's palace
solution: ARYABHATA's contributions included stating that the EARTH ROTATES on its AXIS and correctly EXPLAINING the CAUSE of ECLIPSES (as shadows, not mythical events) — remarkable scientific insights. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The concept of 'zero' and the decimal place-value system are important because they:
options: Revolutionised mathematics and are the basis of modern arithmetic worldwide
solution: The concept of ZERO and the DECIMAL PLACE-VALUE system are important because they REVOLUTIONISED MATHEMATICS and are the BASIS of MODERN ARITHMETIC WORLDWIDE — one of India's greatest contributions to knowledge. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Kalidasa is best known as a master of:
solution: KALIDASA is best known as a master of SANSKRIT POETRY and DRAMA — his works like Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta are classics of world literature. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The account of Fa-Hien (Faxian) is valuable because it describes:
options: The society, religion and conditions of Gupta India as seen by a foreign visitor
solution: FA-HIEN's ACCOUNT is valuable because it DESCRIBES the SOCIETY, RELIGION, and CONDITIONS of GUPTA INDIA as seen by a FOREIGN (Chinese Buddhist) VISITOR — an important outside source. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Samudragupta — Prayaga Prashasti 2. Chandragupta II — Vikramaditya 3. Aryabhata — Aryabhatiya. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE are correct: SAMUDRAGUPTA → the PRAYAGA PRASHASTI (by Harishena); CHANDRAGUPTA II → the title VIKRAMADITYA; and ARYABHATA → the ARYABHATIYA. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta rulers minted beautiful coins made of:
solution: The GUPTA rulers minted beautiful COINS made of GOLD (and some silver), often depicting the kings in various poses — reflecting their wealth and artistry. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Iron Pillar of Delhi, famous for not rusting, dates from around the Gupta period and shows their advanced:
solution: The IRON PILLAR of DELHI, which has NOT RUSTED for over 1,500 years, dates from around the Gupta period and shows their ADVANCED METALLURGY (iron-working skills). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The medical knowledge of ancient India, developed and preserved in this era, is associated with texts by:
solution: Ancient Indian MEDICAL KNOWLEDGE is associated with texts by CHARAKA (on MEDICINE) and SUSHRUTA (on SURGERY) — foundational works of Ayurveda, refined and preserved in this era. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The astronomer Varahamihira of this period is known for his work on:
options: Astronomy, astrology and natural sciences (the Brihat Samhita)
solution: VARAHAMIHIRA is known for his work on ASTRONOMY, ASTROLOGY, and the NATURAL SCIENCES — his encyclopaedic BRIHAT SAMHITA covered many subjects. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The famous Buddhist cave paintings at Ajanta reached a high point of artistry during and around the:
solution: The famous BUDDHIST CAVE PAINTINGS at AJANTA reached a high point of artistry during and around the GUPTA period — masterpieces of ancient Indian painting. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The prosperity of the Gupta empire was based on:
options: Agriculture, trade (inland and overseas) and crafts
solution: The PROSPERITY of the GUPTA empire was based on AGRICULTURE, flourishing TRADE (both inland and overseas), and thriving CRAFTS — funding its cultural achievements. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Gupta age is called a Golden Age. Reason (R): It saw outstanding achievements in art, literature, science and mathematics. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Gupta age is called a Golden Age. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: it saw OUTSTANDING ACHIEVEMENTS in ART, LITERATURE, SCIENCE, and MATHEMATICS — which is precisely why it earned the name. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Samudragupta's conquests are described in an inscription engraved on which pillar?
options: The Allahabad (Prayaga) Pillar — an older Ashokan pillar
solution: SAMUDRAGUPTA's CONQUESTS are described in the PRAYAGA PRASHASTI, engraved on the ALLAHABAD (Prayaga) PILLAR — an OLDER ASHOKAN pillar reused for the Gupta inscription. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Nalanda, which flourished around and after this period, was a famous:
solution: NALANDA was a famous CENTRE of LEARNING — an ancient university that attracted students and scholars from across Asia, flourishing around and after the Gupta period. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta administration was:
options: Well organised, with provinces, officials and a fair revenue system
solution: The GUPTA administration was WELL ORGANISED, with the empire divided into PROVINCES governed by OFFICIALS and supported by a FAIR REVENUE system — though it allowed considerable local autonomy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The literature of the Gupta period was written mainly in which language?
solution: The LITERATURE of the GUPTA period was written mainly in SANSKRIT, which flourished as the language of poetry, drama, science, and philosophy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The sculpture of the Gupta period is admired for its:
options: Grace, balance and refined depiction of deities and the Buddha
solution: GUPTA SCULPTURE is admired for its GRACE, BALANCE, and REFINED DEPICTION of DEITIES and the BUDDHA — considered a high point of classical Indian art. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The decline of the Gupta empire was hastened by:
options: Invasions by the Hunas and internal weaknesses
solution: The DECLINE of the GUPTA empire was hastened by INVASIONS by the HUNAS (a Central Asian people) and by INTERNAL WEAKNESSES and the rise of feudatories. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta ruler who successfully resisted the early Huna invasions was:
solution: SKANDAGUPTA is remembered for successfully RESISTING the EARLY HUNA INVASIONS, protecting the empire for a time before its eventual decline. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The achievements of the Gupta age in science and mathematics show that ancient India was:
options: Highly advanced in knowledge and made contributions still valued today
solution: The GUPTA achievements in SCIENCE and MATHEMATICS show that ancient India was HIGHLY ADVANCED in KNOWLEDGE and made CONTRIBUTIONS (like zero and the decimal system) STILL VALUED TODAY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a Gupta-era figure with their field?
options: Kalidasa → literature; Aryabhata → mathematics/astronomy; Sushruta → surgery
Kalidasa → surgery; Aryabhata → poetry; Sushruta → astronomy
solution: The correct pairings are: KALIDASA → LITERATURE; ARYABHATA → MATHEMATICS/ASTRONOMY; and SUSHRUTA → SURGERY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta rulers followed a policy that allowed:
options: Local rulers and regions considerable autonomy under Gupta overlordship
Total central control of every village
solution: The GUPTA rulers followed a policy that allowed LOCAL RULERS and REGIONS considerable AUTONOMY under GUPTA OVERLORDSHIP — a more decentralised system than the Mauryan empire. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'Aryabhatiya' is significant because it:
options: Is a foundational text of Indian mathematics and astronomy
solution: The ARYABHATIYA (by ARYABHATA) is significant because it is a FOUNDATIONAL TEXT of Indian MATHEMATICS and ASTRONOMY, containing pioneering ideas on numbers, the Earth's rotation, and eclipses. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The temples of the Gupta period mark the beginning of:
options: Structural (free-standing) stone temple architecture in India
solution: The TEMPLES of the GUPTA period mark the BEGINNING of STRUCTURAL (free-standing) STONE TEMPLE ARCHITECTURE in India — the roots of later grand temple styles. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about the Gupta era?
options: It combined political stability with a flowering of culture, science and art
It was a time of no achievement
solution: It is TRUE that the GUPTA ERA combined POLITICAL STABILITY (a strong empire) with a FLOWERING of CULTURE, SCIENCE, and ART — the reason it is remembered as a golden age. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The spread of Indian knowledge (mathematics, astronomy, art) to other lands in this era shows that India was:
options: A major contributor to world civilisation
solution: The SPREAD of INDIAN KNOWLEDGE (mathematics, astronomy, art) to other lands shows that India was a MAJOR CONTRIBUTOR to WORLD CIVILISATION, giving as well as receiving ideas. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta empire arose in which region as its power base?
solution: The GUPTA EMPIRE arose in MAGADHA (the fertile GANGA PLAINS) as its power base, the same heartland from which the Mauryas had ruled. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The value of the number system with zero is that it allows:
options: Easy writing and calculation of very large numbers using place value
solution: The number system with ZERO and PLACE VALUE allows EASY WRITING and CALCULATION of VERY LARGE NUMBERS — a huge advance over older systems, and the foundation of modern maths. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta age is well documented thanks to sources such as:
options: Inscriptions, coins, literature and foreign travellers' accounts
solution: The GUPTA age is well documented thanks to INSCRIPTIONS (like the Prayaga Prashasti), COINS, LITERATURE, and FOREIGN TRAVELLERS' ACCOUNTS (like Fa-Hien's). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The patronage of scholars, poets and artists by Gupta rulers shows that they:
options: Valued learning and culture, encouraging their growth
solution: The PATRONAGE of scholars, poets, and artists by GUPTA rulers shows that they VALUED LEARNING and CULTURE, ENCOURAGING their GROWTH — a key reason for the age's creativity. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The trade of the Gupta period connected India to:
options: Southeast Asia, China and the West by land and sea
solution: The TRADE of the GUPTA period connected India to SOUTHEAST ASIA, CHINA, and the WEST by both LAND and SEA — spreading goods, ideas, and Indian culture. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The advances in astronomy in this period helped in:
options: Understanding eclipses, the calendar, and the movement of planets
solution: The ADVANCES in ASTRONOMY helped in UNDERSTANDING ECLIPSES, refining the CALENDAR, and studying the MOVEMENT of PLANETS — practical and scientific achievements. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The refined Sanskrit dramas and poems of the Gupta age dealt with themes such as:
solution: The refined SANSKRIT DRAMAS and POEMS of the Gupta age dealt with themes like LOVE, NATURE, HEROISM, and MYTHOLOGY — as in Kalidasa's celebrated works. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gupta gold coins are useful to historians because they:
options: Show the rulers, their titles and activities, and reflect the empire's wealth
solution: The GUPTA GOLD COINS are useful because they SHOW the RULERS, their TITLES and ACTIVITIES (like playing the veena or performing rituals), and REFLECT the empire's WEALTH. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The tolerance of the Gupta rulers towards different religions meant that:
options: Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism all flourished during their rule
solution: The TOLERANCE of the GUPTA rulers meant that HINDUISM (which they especially favoured), BUDDHISM, and JAINISM ALL FLOURISHED during their rule — a period of religious coexistence and vitality. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The lasting legacy of the Gupta age includes:
options: Contributions to mathematics, science, art and literature that influence the world today
solution: The lasting LEGACY of the GUPTA age includes CONTRIBUTIONS to MATHEMATICS (zero, decimals), SCIENCE, ART, and LITERATURE that INFLUENCE the WORLD TODAY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The title 'Vikramaditya' taken by Chandragupta II means:
options: 'Sun of valour/prowess' — a title of a heroic king
solution: The title VIKRAMADITYA means 'SUN of VALOUR/PROWESS' — a title befitting a HEROIC KING, taken by Chandragupta II at the height of Gupta power. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is the Gupta period important for the history of Indian science?
options: It produced pioneering work in mathematics, astronomy and medicine still remembered today
solution: The GUPTA period is important for Indian science because it PRODUCED PIONEERING WORK in MATHEMATICS (Aryabhata), ASTRONOMY (Varahamihira), and MEDICINE (Charaka, Sushruta) that is STILL REMEMBERED TODAY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity' is that:
options: The GUPTA EMPIRE (from about the 4th century CE, with its capital at PATALIPUTRA) was a time of political stability and a great flowering of culture — often called the 'GOLDEN AGE' of ancient India; rulers like SAMUDRAGUPTA (the 'Napoleon of India', praised in the Prayaga Prashasti) and CHANDRAGUPTA II ('Vikramaditya', in whose reign Fa-Hien visited) built a strong, well-run empire; the age produced KALIDASA in literature, ARYABHATA and VARAHAMIHIRA in mathematics and astronomy (the concept of ZERO, the decimal system, the Earth's rotation), CHARAKA and SUSHRUTA in medicine and surgery, fine gold coins, temples, sculpture and the Ajanta paintings — a tireless creativity that made lasting contributions to world civilisation, before the empire declined under Huna invasions
It was a dark, empty age
India had no science or art
solution: The chapter's overall message is that the GUPTA EMPIRE (rising from about the 4th century CE, with its capital at PATALIPUTRA) was a time of POLITICAL STABILITY and a GREAT FLOWERING of CULTURE — often called the 'GOLDEN AGE' of ancient India. Rulers like SAMUDRAGUPTA (nicknamed the 'NAPOLEON of INDIA', whose conquests are praised in the PRAYAGA PRASHASTI by Harishena) and CHANDRAGUPTA II ('VIKRAMADITYA', in whose reign the Chinese pilgrim FA-HIEN visited) built a STRONG, WELL-RUN empire. The age produced KALIDASA in LITERATURE, ARYABHATA and VARAHAMIHIRA in MATHEMATICS and ASTRONOMY (the concept of ZERO, the DECIMAL place-value system, and the idea that the EARTH ROTATES), CHARAKA and SUSHRUTA in MEDICINE and SURGERY, along with fine GOLD COINS, the beginnings of STONE TEMPLE architecture, superb SCULPTURE, and the AJANTA PAINTINGS — a TIRELESS CREATIVITY that made LASTING CONTRIBUTIONS to WORLD CIVILISATION, before the empire DECLINED under the HUNA invasions. So the overall message is option 2.
